items.value: This policy explains what personal data Digitorium collects, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it and what you can ask us to do with it. It is written for India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (the DPDP Act) and the rules made under it, the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011.

Digitorium is a sole proprietorship of Neel Surti, based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. We build websites and software, run Meta and Google ads, and do SEO, shoots and branding. For the personal data described here, we are the "Data Fiduciary" under the DPDP Act, which means we decide why and how it is used.

We do not sell your personal data, and we do not use it for anything unrelated to these purposes.

When you fill in our consultation form or click Accept on the cookie banner, you consent to the use of your data for the purposes stated there. When you send us your details yourself to get a quote or a service, we may also rely on the "legitimate uses" allowed by Section 7 of the DPDP Act.

We may also disclose personal data if an Indian law, court or government authority requires it. We never share your details with other businesses for their own marketing.

Consultation form submissions are stored in a Supabase database hosted in Tokyo, Japan. Our website is served by Vercel from servers around the world. Meta and Google process data on their own servers, which may be outside India. The DPDP Act allows personal data to be processed outside India except in countries the Government of India restricts, and we will stop using any location that becomes restricted.

As required by the Information Technology Act, 2000 and its rules, and by the DPDP Act, questions and complaints about your personal data go to our Grievance Officer:
10 Mangalmay Complex, Maninagar, Ahmedabad, Gujarat 380008, India
We will resolve your complaint within one month of receiving it. If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India under the DPDP Act.

We follow reasonable security practices as required by Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The whole site runs over an encrypted HTTPS connection. The consultation form can only add new entries to our database: nobody visiting the site can read, change or delete them. Access to our accounts is limited to the people who need it. No system is perfectly secure, and if a breach affects your personal data, we will tell you and the Data Protection Board of India as the DPDP Act requires.
Our services are for businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18. If you believe a child has sent us their details, email us and we will delete them.

If we change how we handle personal data, we will update this page and the date at the top. If the change is significant, for example a new purpose or a new kind of data, we will ask for your consent again where the law requires it.
